summary: All six acceptance criteria verified by code inspection. The error div placement, OR-fallback in csShowTableError(), revert swap, catch-block ordering, and csReorderMode comment update are all correct.

The ordering comment inside the catch block ('Re-render first so #cs-reorder-error exists before csShowTableError() writes to it.') is a valuable explicit documentation of a non-obvious DOM-dependency invariant.
The OR-fallback pattern (getElementById('cs-table-error') || getElementById('cs-reorder-error')) is clean, view-agnostic, and forward-compatible with any future view state that needs error reporting.
csShowTableError() called outside the contentEl guard is a minor consistency gap (safe no-op path), logged as a low-priority improvement. No blocking issues. 3947/3947 tests pass.

comments.note: The explicit ordering comment inside the catch block ('Re-render first so #cs-reorder-error exists before csShowTableError() writes to it.') is exactly right for this kind of subtle DOM-dependency constraint. Without it, a future refactor could silently break the invariant by reordering the two calls. This is the correct documentation approach.

csShowTableError() is called unconditionally outside the `if (contentEl)` guard in the catch block, while the re-render is inside the guard. If contentEl is null, the error div is never created, so csShowTableError() silently no-ops (getElementById returns null, showError is not called). The behavior is safe but slightly inconsistent with the surrounding guard pattern. For strict symmetry, csShowTableError() could also live inside the contentEl guard. Not blocking — the no-op path is acceptable.
